paper_title: Breaking the Softmax Bottleneck: A High-Rank RNN Language Model

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for its proposed model without dynamic evaluation?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports a test perplexity of 55.97 for AWD-LSTM-MoS without finetune and 54.44 for AWD-LSTM-MoS with finetune, both without dynamic evaluation.
sub_questions.quote: Ours – AWD-LSTM-MoS w/o finetune 22M 58.08 55.97; Ours – AWD-LSTM-MoS 22M 56.54 54.44

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for its proposed model with dynamic evaluation?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports a test perplexity of 47.69 for AWD-LSTM-MoS with dynamic evaluation.

sub_questions.q: Does the paper report results for its proposed model on Penn Treebank using cache/pointer or ensemble methods?
sub_questions.answer: No, the paper does not report results for its proposed model using cache/pointer or ensemble methods on Penn Treebank; it only reports results with and without dynamic evaluation and finetuning.

sub_questions.q: What baseline test perplexities on Penn Treebank does the paper list for comparison?
sub_questions.answer: The paper lists baseline test perplexities on Penn Treebank including 92.0 (RNN-LDA + KN-5 + cache), 82.7 (LSTM), 78.6 (Variational LSTM), 78.9 (CharCNN), 70.9 (Pointer Sentinel-LSTM), 72.1 (LSTM + continuous cache pointer), 73.2 (Tied Variational LSTM + augmented loss), 65.4 (Variational RHN), 64.0 (NAS Cell), 58.3 (2-layer skip connection LSTM), 58.8 (AWD-LSTM w/o finetune), 57.3 (AWD-LSTM), 52.8 (AWD-LSTM + continuous cache pointer), and 51.1 (AWD-LSTM + dynamic evaluation).
sub_questions.quote: Mikolov & Zweig 2012 – RNN-LDA + KN-5 + cache 9M‡ - 92.0; ... Krause et al. 2017 – AWD-LSTM + dynamic evaluation † 24M 51.6 51.1

sub_questions.q: How does the proposed model's Penn Treebank test perplexity compare to the baselines listed in the paper?
sub_questions.answer: The proposed model's test perplexity of 47.69 (with dynamic evaluation) is lower than all listed baselines, including the best baseline of 51.1 (AWD-LSTM + dynamic evaluation), improving by 3.41 points. Without dynamic evaluation, the proposed model achieves 54.44 (with finetune) and 55.97 (without finetune), which are lower than corresponding baselines like AWD-LSTM (57.3) and AWD-LSTM w/o finetune (58.8).
sub_questions.quote: With a comparable number of parameters, MoS outperforms all baselines with or without dynamic evaluation, and substantially improves over the current state of the art, by up to 3.6 points in perplexity.
